title: Coworker Conflict
locationRef: A small glass-walled meeting room. You've both been asked to resolve a project disagreement.
setup: Morgan sits across from you with crossed arms. There's unresolved tension after last month's miscommunication.
storyPlot: Last month, something went wrong on the Henderson project — deadlines were missed, blame got passed around, and you and Morgan ended up on opposite sides of a very tense email chain. You're not sure who was more at fault. Your manager has now put you both in a meeting room together with one instruction: sort it out. Morgan got here first and chose the seat that faces the door. The room is small and glass-walled, visible to the rest of the office. Whatever happens in the next few minutes, everyone will be able to see — if not hear — how it goes.
openingLine: Morgan glances at the door, then back at you. 'So. Are we going to talk about what happened, or are we pretending it's fine?'
successCondition: Composite score ≥ 70 and de-escalation acknowledged in dialogue
failureCondition: Composite score < 40 OR mood cools three turns in a row
